title: A book with no bend in it.
subtitle: Praise for a guide that does not twist

key.label: What kind of guide it is

row.title: a vague guide
sub: read it any way you like

then: The Quraysh had sent men to ask the rabbis of Madinah for questions to test the Prophet ﷺ. This surah came as the answer, and it opens with praise. Ibn Kathir calls the Book {reward}the greatest blessing Allah gave the people of this earth{/reward}, one with {idea}nothing twisted or confusing{/idea} in it.
now: You scroll through ten opinions on one question and each one bends a little toward what the speaker wants. Advice that shifts with the mood of the room. {idea}Here is a voice that does not bend to please you.{/idea} That is worth praising before anything else.
old: Every source of guidance has some angle to it.
new: This Book has no angle. It is straight, and that is a gift worth thanks.
try: Before you open the Quran today, say Alhamdulillah once for the fact that you have it.

title: Straight, so it can warn and give hope.
subtitle: The two jobs of the Book

key.label: Who the good news is for

then: Ibn Kathir explains that the Book warns those who oppose the Prophet ﷺ and reject the message, and {reward}gives good news to the believers{/reward}. He adds that these believers are those who {idea}confirm their faith by righteous actions{/idea}.
now: You say you believe, and you mean it. Then a coworker asks for help on a long day and you pretend not to see the message. {idea}The good news in this verse is tied to what your hands do{/idea}, not only what your heart holds.
old: Believing is the main thing. Deeds are extra.
new: The verse pairs belief with good deeds. One proves the other.
try: Pick one small good deed that matches something you say you believe, and do it today.

title: A reward that never runs out.
subtitle: What forever means next to what ends
then: This short verse finishes the good news of the one before it. Ibn Kathir says the believers live in what Allah rewards them with, Paradise, {reward}for always, never ending or ceasing to be{/reward}.
now: Payday comes and the money is gone by the 20th. The promotion felt huge for a week. The new phone is old in a year. {idea}Every reward you know has an end date.{/idea} This one does not.
old: Good things are good, but they never last.
new: There is one reward that does not wear out, and small deeds lead to it.
try: Next time something nice ends today, say quietly: the lasting one is still ahead.

title: A special warning for one claim about Allah.
subtitle: Saying Allah has taken a child
then: After the general warning, this verse names one group. Ibn Ishaq said these were {trap}the pagan Arabs who said, we worship the angels who are the daughters of Allah{/trap}. The Book was sent to warn them by name.
now: It is easy to talk about Allah casually. In a heated chat, a sentence starts with: God would never... or God wants me to... {idea}What you say about Allah carries more weight than anything else you say.{/idea}
old: What I say about God is just my opinion.
new: Words about Allah are the heaviest words I speak.
try: Today, when you are about to say what Allah wants or thinks, pause and check if you actually know it.

title: No knowledge, only words handed down.
subtitle: A big claim with nothing under it
then: Ibn Kathir says this claim was {trap}made up, with no basis apart from what they say{/trap}. Their predecessors had no knowledge of it either. The verse calls it a grave word, because it is a lie spoken about Allah.
now: Your family has always done a thing a certain way. Someone asks why and the only answer is: that is how we do it. {idea}Old does not mean true.{/idea} The verse asks a simple question: what do you actually know?
old: If my parents believed it, it is safe to repeat.
new: A claim about Allah needs knowledge, not just a long history.
try: Pick one thing you repeat about religion and find out today where it really comes from.

title: Do not destroy yourself grieving over their choice.
subtitle: Caring for people without carrying their decisions
then: Allah consoles His Messenger ﷺ, who was hurting because his people would not believe. Qatadah said this grief was anger and sorrow, Mujahid said anxiety. The message, Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}just convey the Message{/idea}, and whoever goes astray {trap}strays at his own loss{/trap}.
now: Your brother keeps making the same bad choice. You lie awake rewriting the talk you will have with him. Your chest is tight every time his name lights up your phone. {idea}You can love him and still put down what is not yours to carry.{/idea}
old: If they do not change, I have failed.
new: My job is to care and to speak well. The turning of hearts belongs to Allah.
try: Make one sincere dua for someone you worry about, then hand the result over to Allah in words.

title: The world is decorated so you can be tested.
subtitle: Adornment with a purpose
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made this world {idea}a place of trial, not a place of settlement{/idea}, adorned with passing beauty. He cites the hadith that the world is {reward}sweet and green{/reward}, and Allah is watching what people will do in it.
now: The new car in the driveway next door. The holiday photos. The kitchen you saw online. None of it is bad. {idea}The question is never how much you got, but what you did with it{/idea}, and the test asks for best deeds, not most things.
old: Life is about collecting the nicest things I can.
new: The nice things are the exam paper. My deeds are the answers.
try: Look at one thing you own that you love. Ask what good you could do with it this week.

title: All the decoration ends as bare dry ground.
subtitle: The same earth, after
then: After describing the world's beauty, Allah says it will pass away. Ibn Abbas said {trap}everything on it would be wiped out{/trap}. Mujahid called it a dry and barren plain, and Qatadah a plain with no trees or vegetation.
now: You have seen an old house cleared out after someone passed away. The furniture they fussed over, sold off in a weekend. The garden overgrown. {idea}What they did for people is what everyone still talks about.{/idea}
old: What I build here will stay.
new: The stage will be cleared. Only what I did on it remains.
try: Spend ten minutes today on something that outlasts objects: a call, a kindness, a prayer for someone.

title: Was the cave really the most amazing sign?
subtitle: Wonder placed in the right size
then: The Quraysh asked about the young men of the cave because the rabbis called it {trap}a strange and wondrous tale{/trap}. Allah answers: compared to creating the heavens and earth and turning night into day, {idea}it is not more amazing{/idea}. Ar-Raqim may be a valley, a town, or a stone tablet at the cave.
now: You will watch a clip of a rare event ten times. The sunrise outside your window this morning got no look at all. {idea}The ordinary miracles are the bigger ones{/idea}, they just come every day.
old: Real signs of Allah are rare, dramatic events.
new: The everyday is full of bigger signs than any rare story.
try: Step outside or open a window today and look at the sky for one full minute.

title: With nowhere left to go, they asked for mercy.
subtitle: The prayer of young men in a cave
then: The young men fled their people {trap}fearing persecution{/trap} for their religion and hid in a mountain cave. Inside, they asked Allah for mercy and to {idea}direct their matter well{/idea}, meaning, grant us a good end.
now: You left the job, or the friendship, or the place, because staying meant losing something of your faith. Now you sit in a small flat with no plan. {idea}You do not need the whole map. You can ask for mercy and a good end.{/idea}
old: I cannot pray about this until I know what to ask for.
new: Ask for mercy and for the outcome to be right. Allah knows the details.
try: Say their dua today about one unclear thing in your life: Our Lord, grant us mercy and set our affair right.

title: The answer to their prayer was sleep.
subtitle: Protection that looked like nothing happening
then: Right after their prayer, Allah says He covered their hearing in the cave. Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}He caused them to sleep when they entered the cave{/reward}, and {idea}they slept for many years{/idea}.
now: You prayed for a way out and what came was a long pause. Nothing moved. No call back, no change. {idea}Sometimes the answer is to be kept safe while time does its work.{/idea}
old: If nothing is happening, my prayer was not answered.
new: A quiet, protected season can be the answer itself.
try: Think of one season of waiting in your life and ask what it may have protected you from.

title: They woke up, and people argued about the time.
subtitle: Two groups counting the years
then: Allah raised them up from their long sleep, and one of them later went out with silver coins to buy food. Ibn Kathir says the verse refers to the two parties who disputed about them, over {idea}how long they stayed in the cave{/idea}.
now: A family group chat erupts over a date, a detail, who said what years ago. Everyone is certain. {idea}Only Allah holds the full record{/idea}, and some arguments are not worth winning.
old: I need to be the one who has the exact detail right.
new: Allah knows the full count. The lesson matters more than the number.
try: Next time a small factual argument starts today, let it go and steer back to what matters.

title: Young people who believed, and were given more guidance.
subtitle: Faith that grows when you step toward it
then: Now the full story begins. Ibn Kathir notes they were {idea}young men, more accepting of the truth{/idea} than elders set in their ways, just as most who first followed the Prophet ﷺ were young. Scholars took from this verse that {reward}faith may increase{/reward} and vary in degrees.
now: You are the only one at the family table who prays on time, or the only one at work who does not join in. You feel small. {idea}The first step was yours. The increase comes from Allah.{/idea}
old: My faith is what it is. I cannot change its level.
new: When I step toward Allah, He adds guidance. Faith grows.
try: Add one small act of worship today, two extra rakahs or one page of Quran, and notice how it feels.

title: Allah tied their hearts firm, then they stood up.
subtitle: Courage that was given, not built

row.title: they stood
sub: our Lord is the Lord of all

then: Ibn Kathir reports they were said to be sons of leaders who left a life of luxury and ease. Called before an arrogant king, {idea}they told him the truth and called him to Allah{/idea}. Allah says He {reward}gave them the patience to go against their people{/reward}.
now: Your manager asks you to fudge the numbers. Your heart is racing in the meeting room. You think you are not the brave type. {idea}Firmness is something Allah gives in the moment you choose to stand.{/idea}
old: I am not strong enough to say no to people with power.
new: Allah ties the heart firm for the one who stands up for Him.
try: Before one hard conversation today, ask Allah quietly to make your heart firm.

title: Where is the proof for what everyone worships?
subtitle: The young men ask for clear authority
then: Standing before their people, the young men asked {idea}why do they not produce some clear evidence and genuine proof{/idea} for their worship. Then they named the deeper wrong: {trap}inventing a lie against Allah{/trap}.
now: A whole office treats money, status, or what people think as the thing that decides everything. You start to bow to it too. {idea}Ask where the proof is that this thing deserves your devotion.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me serves it, it must deserve it.
new: A crowd is not proof. What do I actually have evidence for?
try: Name one thing you give too much of your heart to, and ask honestly what proof it deserves that.

title: Step away, and Allah will spread His mercy for you.
subtitle: Leaving with trust, not a plan
then: The king gave them time to think, hoping they would return to their old religion. Ibn Kathir says that delay {reward}was a way Allah showed kindness to them{/reward}, because they used it to escape. They told one another: withdraw from them, go to the cave, and {idea}your Lord will open a way for you from His mercy{/idea}.
now: You leave a friend group that pulls you away from prayer. Friday nights are suddenly quiet. Your room feels like a cave. {idea}The space you made for Allah is where His mercy can spread.{/idea}
old: If I step away, I will be left alone with nothing.
new: Stepping away for Allah opens room for His mercy, even in a small cave.
try: Step away from one thing tonight that pulls you from Allah, and spend that time with Him.

title: The sun bent its path around them.
subtitle: Quiet care in the details
then: Ibn Kathir explains the sun entered the cave {reward}without touching them{/reward}, since direct light would have burnt them, while sun and air helped preserve them. He notes Allah described the cave but {idea}did not tell us where it is, because there is no benefit in knowing that{/idea}.
now: You spend an evening reading forum threads about exact locations and dates in a story. Meanwhile the point of the story sits untouched. {idea}Allah tells you what helps you, and leaves out what does not.{/idea}
old: I need every detail before the story means anything.
new: The sign is the care Allah showed. The rest is trivia.
try: Next time you read a Quran story, write one sentence on what it teaches you, not where it happened.

title: Even their dog shared in their blessing.
subtitle: Kept safe, turned, and guarded

row.title: famous forever
sub: because of who he stayed with

then: Ibn Abbas said if they had not been turned over, the earth would have consumed them. Their dog lay at the door as if guarding them. Ibn Kathir says {reward}the blessing they enjoyed extended to their dog{/reward}, and calls this {idea}the benefit of accompanying good people{/idea}.
now: The friend who drags you to the masjid on a Friday when you would rather sleep in. The colleague whose honesty makes you a little more honest. {idea}Who you sit with shapes what you become, and what you share in.{/idea}
old: My friends do not really change who I am.
new: Staying near good people spreads their blessing onto me.
try: Send a message today to one person who makes you better, and plan time with them.

title: Not sure how long? Then move on to what matters.
subtitle: Waking up and getting on with it

row.title: how long?
sub: a day or part of one

then: After 309 years they woke and asked how long they had slept. Unsure, they said {idea}your Lord knows best{/idea}, then turned to more pressing matters. They sent one with their silver coins to find the {reward}purest food{/reward}, and told him to be careful.
now: You wake up after a hard season, a loss or an illness, and spend days asking how you lost so much time. {idea}Hand the question to Allah and take the next good step.{/idea} Even if that step is just a clean, simple meal.
old: I cannot move on until I understand exactly what happened.
new: Some questions go to Allah. My job is the next good step.
try: Write down one question you keep circling, say Allahu alam, and do one practical task instead.

title: Losing your faith is worse than losing your safety.
subtitle: What the young men feared most
then: They feared the followers of Decianus might find them and {trap}torture them until they went back to their former religion{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says that if they agreed to go back, {idea}they would never attain success in this world or the Hereafter{/idea}.
now: Pressure rarely looks like stones today. It looks like a steady drip: jokes at your expense, an invite that clashes with prayer, a quiet push to be less visible. {idea}The real danger is slowly being turned back.{/idea}
old: Small compromises with my faith are no big deal if they keep the peace.
new: Being turned back from faith is the loss that never heals.
try: Notice one small compromise you have been making, and hold your ground on it once today.

title: Their discovery became proof that the Hour is real.
subtitle: A sign for people who doubted resurrection
then: Ikrimah said some people then believed souls would rise but not bodies, {idea}so Allah resurrected the people of the Cave as a sign{/idea}. When the coin was passed around the market, the story came out. Then {trap}people disputed over what to build over them{/trap}, and Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ warned against taking the graves of the righteous as places of worship.
now: You read about a miracle and the comments section is all about the building, the place, the souvenir. {idea}Allah's sign is pointing past all of that{/idea}: you will be raised too.
old: Death is the end of the body.
new: The One who woke them after centuries will wake me too.
try: Tonight before sleep, remember that waking up is a small rehearsal of being raised.

title: Three, five, or seven: leave the count to Allah.
subtitle: Guessing at the unseen
then: People disputed the number. Allah calls the first two views {trap}guessing at the unseen{/trap}, like shooting at a target you cannot see, and leaves the third uncorrected. Ibn Abbas said they were seven. Ibn Kathir draws the lesson: {idea}the best thing is to refer knowledge to Allah{/idea}, and debate gently if at all.
now: A heated thread online about a detail nobody can prove. You have your fingers ready to type a long reply. {idea}Say what you know, say Allah knows best, and close the app.{/idea}
old: If I have an opinion, I should defend it to the end.
new: Where knowledge ends, I say Allah knows best and stop.
try: Skip one argument today about something nobody can really know.

title: Never say I will do it tomorrow, by itself.
subtitle: Plans are not promises you control

row.title: Allah
sub: Knower of what is to be

then: When the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the people of the Cave, he said, {trap}I will tell you tomorrow{/trap}, without adding If Allah wills, and the revelation was delayed for fifteen days. Here Allah teaches him that plans for the future {idea}should always be referred to the will of Allah{/idea}.
now: Your phone calendar is full: gym at 6, report due Thursday, trip in March. It all feels certain. {idea}Every square on that screen belongs to Allah first.{/idea}
old: If it is planned, it will happen.
new: My plans are real, and every one of them waits on Allah's will.
try: Say In sha Allah, sincerely and not as a brush-off, each time you talk about tomorrow today.

title: Forgot to say If Allah wills? Remember Him now.
subtitle: A door back when you slip

row.title: say it when you remember
sub: and ask for a nearer way

then: Abu Al-Aliyah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said this means: {reward}if you forget to say If Allah wills, say it when you remember{/reward}. The verse adds a prayer for when you do not know something: {idea}perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer to right{/idea}.
now: You promised your kid you would be home early, said it like a fact, and only thought of Allah on the drive. {idea}It is not too late to turn your heart back to Him.{/idea} The door does not shut because you forgot.
old: I forgot, so it no longer counts.
new: Remembering late is still remembering. Allah welcomes it.
try: When you notice you forgot to remember Allah today, simply pause and remember Him right then.

title: Three hundred years, and nine more.
subtitle: The exact length of their sleep
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the length was {idea}three hundred plus nine years in lunar years, which is three hundred in solar years{/idea}. Ibn Jarir held that Allah is stating the fact here, {reward}not just repeating what people said{/reward}.
now: You feel the years slipping. Ten years at the same job, a decade since you said you would learn to read Quran properly. {idea}Allah has counted every one of those years, and none of them are lost to Him.{/idea}
old: Long stretches of my life just blur and vanish.
new: Allah keeps exact count of every year, even the ones I slept through.
try: Pick one good intention you have delayed for years and do a first five minutes of it today.

title: He sees and hears it all, and rules alone.
subtitle: The close of the Cave story
then: The story ends by returning everything to Allah. If asked about it without knowledge, say {idea}Allah knows best how long they stayed{/idea}. Qatadah said: {reward}no one hears or sees more than Allah{/reward}. He has no adviser, supporter, or partner.
now: You lie awake in a hospital corridor chair, sure that nobody sees how hard this is. {idea}He sees you. He hears every whispered word.{/idea} And no one else holds the final say over what happens next.
old: Nobody really sees what I am going through.
new: Allah sees and hears all of it, and He is the One who decides.
try: Tell Allah one thing today you have not told anyone, knowing He already hears it.

title: Recite it as it came. No one can change His words.
subtitle: The only real shelter
then: Right after the questions of the Quraysh, Allah commands His Messenger ﷺ to recite and convey His Book. {idea}No one can alter, distort, or misinterpret His words.{/idea} Mujahid said the refuge meant {reward}a shelter{/reward}, Qatadah said a helper or supporter.
now: Someone at work hears you are Muslim and asks a hard question. The easy move is to trim the answer so it goes down smoothly. {idea}You do not have to reshape His words to be safe.{/idea} He is the shelter.
old: I should adjust what the Quran says so people accept it.
new: His words stand as they are. My safety is with Him, not with approval.
try: Read one passage of Quran today slowly, as it is, without rushing to explain it away.

title: Stay with the ones who call on Allah morning and evening.
subtitle: Choosing company over glitter
then: The nobles of Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ to sit with them alone, {trap}without his weak Companions{/trap} like Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab and Ibn Masud. Allah forbade it. Ibn Abbas explained: {idea}do not seek the people of nobility and wealth instead of them{/idea}.
now: At the wedding you drift toward the table with the important people and away from the old uncle who prays in the corner. {idea}Your eyes are being tested on who they find worth looking at.{/idea}
old: Time with influential people is time well spent.
new: Time with people who remember Allah is the company worth keeping.
try: Sit with someone overlooked at your masjid or workplace today, and actually listen.

title: The truth is clear. Your choice carries its end.
subtitle: Free will with real consequences
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say that what he brought is {idea}the truth, in which there is no confusion or doubt{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains that the words whoever wills, let him believe are {trap}a type of threat and stern warning{/trap}. The verse then describes, in hard terms, the place prepared for wrongdoers.
now: Every app tells you every choice is fine, just personal preference. {idea}This verse respects your freedom and refuses to pretend it has no weight.{/idea} Today's small choices are steps toward one of two places.
old: As long as it is my choice, it cannot be wrong.
new: My choice is free, and that is exactly why it matters so much.
try: Make one choice today slowly, asking which way it moves you, then pick the better way.

title: No good deed done well is ever lost.
subtitle: The other side of the warning
then: Right after describing the doomed, Allah turns to {reward}the blessed who believed{/reward} and did the righteous deeds the Messengers taught. The promise is that the reward of anyone who {idea}does his deeds in the most perfect manner{/idea} will not be lost.
now: You washed the dishes nobody thanked you for. You stayed patient with a difficult parent on the phone. You gave quietly and no one knew. {idea}Every one of those is safe with Allah.{/idea}
old: If no one sees my effort, it was wasted.
new: Effort done well for Allah is never wasted, seen or not.
try: Do one small task today with real care, as if it is the deed you will be shown.

title: Gardens that last, and an excellent place to rest.
subtitle: What patience is waiting for
then: Ibn Kathir notes Adn means {reward}lasting{/reward}. He points out the contrast: Hell was called an evil Murtafaq, a place to rest, and Paradise here is {idea}an excellent place to dwell and rest and stay{/idea}.
now: You are worn out. Long shifts, sleepless nights with a baby, a body that aches. Rest feels like a luxury. {idea}A resting place is being prepared for those who keep going for Allah.{/idea}
old: I will never truly get to rest.
new: There is a real, lasting rest ahead for the believer who keeps going.
try: Take five quiet minutes today, and use them to ask Allah for the rest that lasts.

title: A story of two men and two gardens.
subtitle: A parable for those who boast
then: After the idolators who were {trap}too arrogant to sit with the poor and weak{/trap} among Muslims, Allah gives them a parable. One man was given two gardens of grapes, ringed with palms and fields, {reward}abundantly fruitful{/reward}.
now: You scroll past someone's perfect house tour and feel small, or you post your own and feel big. {idea}This story is about both of those feelings.{/idea} Watch which man you become.
old: Stories about wealth are about other, richer people.
new: This parable is a mirror for anyone who has been given something.
try: List three blessings you have that someone near you lacks. Thank Allah for each, quietly.

title: Every tree gave fruit, and a river ran through.
subtitle: When everything is going right
then: Ibn Kathir says each garden {reward}produced its fruits and nothing at all was diminishing{/reward}. The verse uses Allah's own voice: {idea}We caused a river to gush forth{/idea}. The success was a gift from the start.
now: Your business has a good year. The kids are healthy, the bills are paid, the car runs. {idea}That is the moment this verse is talking about{/idea}: when it is easy to forget Who made the river flow.
old: When things go well, it is because I did well.
new: When things go well, Allah is the One making the river run.
try: Name one thing going well right now and say: this is from Allah.

title: I have more than you: the boast.
subtitle: Comparing wealth and entourage
then: While they were talking, the garden owner was {trap}disputing, boasting and showing off{/trap}. He meant he had more servants, attendants and children. Qatadah said: {trap}this, by Allah, is the wish of the immoral{/trap}, a lot of wealth and a large entourage.
now: Followers, salary, the school your kids attend. The quiet scoreboard you keep in your head when you meet an old friend. {idea}The verse catches you the moment you start comparing.{/idea}
old: Having more than others means I am doing better than them.
new: More wealth is not more worth. The scoreboard I keep is the wrong one.
try: Next time you catch yourself comparing today, say Ma sha Allah for the other person instead.

title: Walking in his garden, he wronged himself.
subtitle: The thought that this will never end
then: Ibn Kathir says he was {trap}allowing himself to be deceived{/trap} by the plants, fruits and rivers he saw, thinking they could never end. The cause was a lack of understanding, weak faith, and being {trap}enamored with this world{/trap}.
now: A good job, good health, a full house. You quietly build your life as if this is how it will always be. {idea}The wrong is not the garden. It is believing it is forever.{/idea}
old: What I have now will always be here.
new: Everything I have is passing. Thinking otherwise wrongs my own soul.
try: Look at something you love today and remind yourself gently that it is on loan.

title: If there is a next life, I will get even better.
subtitle: Mistaking blessings for being special

row.title: even better for me
sub: I must be dear to Him

row.title: Allah is testing me
sub: look what I do with it

then: He doubted the Hour would come. Then he said if he was returned to his Lord, he would get better still. Ibn Kathir explains his logic: {trap}if I were not dear to Him, He would not have given me all this{/trap}. He {trap}took it for granted, without any sound evidence{/trap}.
now: A promotion, a nice house, an easy life, and a small voice says: Allah must be pleased with me. {idea}Ease is not a certificate.{/idea} Earlier in this surah, adornment was called a test.
old: If life is easy for me, Allah must be pleased with me.
new: What I have is a test of what I do, not proof of my rank.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: what am I doing with the ease I have been given?

title: Remember you were dust, then a drop.
subtitle: The poor friend's reply
then: His believing companion answered by {idea}warning and rebuking him{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says everyone knows {idea}he was nothing, then he came to be{/idea}, and that his existence is not due to himself or any other creature.
now: You hear yourself say I built this from nothing at a dinner. Your hands did work, true. {idea}But someone gave you the hands, the breath, the very start.{/idea}
old: I am self-made.
new: I was made. Everything I built started with what He gave me.
try: Before you talk about your success today, thank Allah for the first gift: your life.

title: But as for me, Allah is my Lord.
subtitle: Standing apart without a garden

row.title: his own clear belief
sub: I do not say what you say

then: The poorer man had no garden to point to. Ibn Kathir puts his meaning simply: {idea}I do not say what you say; rather I acknowledge the Oneness and Lordship of Allah{/idea}. He held his ground {reward}with nothing in his hands but faith{/reward}.
now: Your cousin with the big house mocks your choices at the family lunch. You do not have a bank balance to answer with. {idea}You do not need one. You can say calmly: but as for me.{/idea}
old: I cannot speak up until I have something to show.
new: Faith speaks with full weight, even from empty hands.
try: In one conversation today, say what you believe calmly, without needing to win.

title: Why did you not say Ma sha Allah?
subtitle: Two phrases for moments of delight
then: The believer asked why, on entering his garden and liking it, he did not praise Allah. One of the Salaf said: {idea}whoever is delighted with something in his wealth or children, let him say Ma sha Allah, la quwwata illa billah{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ called that last phrase {reward}a treasure of Paradise{/reward}.
now: You pull into the driveway of the new house. You hold your newborn. You see your exam result. {idea}That first rush of delight is exactly when to say these words.{/idea}
old: Ma sha Allah is something you say about other people's things.
new: It belongs on my own blessings first, the moment I enjoy them.
try: Say Ma sha Allah, la quwwata illa billah the next time something of yours delights you today.

title: My Lord may give me better, and yours could vanish.
subtitle: Hope for the poor, warning for the proud
then: The believer did not envy him. He hoped Allah would give him {reward}something better than your garden, in the Hereafter{/reward}. He warned that the garden could be struck from the sky, a mighty rain leaving {trap}smooth mud in which one cannot get a foothold{/trap}.
now: You feel behind your friends in money and home. {idea}Hope for better from your Lord is not jealousy.{/idea} And the friend who seems so secure is just as dependent on Allah as you are.
old: They have more, so they are safe and I am behind.
new: My Lord can give me better, and no garden is safe without Him.
try: Ask Allah today for something better in the Hereafter instead of wishing for what someone else has.

title: Or the water sinks away, out of reach.
subtitle: The source you never thought could fail
then: The believer adds a second warning. The water could {trap}disappear into the earth{/trap}, the opposite of water rising to the surface. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: {idea}if your water sank away, who then could bring you flowing water?{/idea}
now: Your salary, your health, the one client who pays the bills. It has always come, so you stopped noticing it. {idea}Every source in your life keeps flowing only because Allah keeps it flowing.{/idea}
old: My income and health are just there. They will keep going.
new: Every source I rely on runs by Allah's permission, every single day.
try: Drink a glass of water slowly today and thank Allah that it reached you.

title: Wringing his hands over a garden collapsed on its trellises.
subtitle: Regret arrives too late
then: What the believer warned of happened. {trap}A storm struck his garden{/trap}, the garden he thought would last forever and that had {trap}distracted him from thoughts of Allah{/trap}. Qatadah said he was clasping his hands in regret and grief for the wealth he had lost.
now: The job you gave every evening to is suddenly cut. The investment collapses. You sit in the car outside the office with your hands over your face. {idea}The real loss was not the money. It was what it had taken the place of.{/idea}
old: Losing this thing is the worst that could happen.
new: Worse is letting a thing take Allah's place in my heart. I can fix that now.
try: Ask: what in my life competes with Allah for my heart? Give Him back one hour from it today.

title: The entourage he bragged about never came.
subtitle: No group to help, no strength of his own
then: Ibn Kathir notes this was the clan and children he had {trap}vainly boasted{/trap} about. When the punishment came, there was no one to save him, and he could not defend himself.
now: You tell yourself you have people. Connections in the right places, a cousin who knows a lawyer. {idea}Good people are a blessing. But none of them can hold back what Allah has decided.{/idea}
old: With the right people behind me, I am protected.
new: People can help only within what Allah allows. He is the real protection.
try: Thank one person who supports you today, and in your heart thank Allah who sent them.

title: In the end, all protection belongs to Allah.
subtitle: The best reward and the best outcome
then: Ibn Kathir says on that day {idea}everyone, believer or disbeliever, will return to Allah{/idea} in allegiance when the punishment comes. Another reading means the rule belongs to Allah, the True God. Deeds done for Him have a {reward}good reward and good consequences{/reward}.
now: You split your trust between your boss, your savings, and your reputation. {idea}One day every loyalty will collapse into one.{/idea} Choosing it now, while it still counts, is the gift.
old: I will sort out my loyalty to Allah later.
new: Everyone turns to Him at the end. Turning now is what earns the best outcome.
try: Do one deed today purely for Allah, telling no one about it.

title: Life is rain, green growth, then dry straw in the wind.
subtitle: The parable of this world
then: After the two gardens, Allah gives a wider parable of {idea}the worldly life, its transient nature and how it will come to an end{/idea}. Rain mixes with seeds, they grow bright and fresh, then {trap}wither, tossed about right and left by the wind{/trap}.
now: Look at a photo of yourself at twenty. That energy, that face, that phase of life felt endless. {idea}It was one season of rain.{/idea} So is this one.
old: I have all the time in the world.
new: This life is a single season. Use the green while it is green.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself today and decide one good thing to do with this season.

title: Wealth and children decorate life. Lasting deeds outlast them.
subtitle: What remains after the straw blows away
then: Ibn Abbas and others said the lasting good deeds are {idea}the five daily prayers{/idea}. He also said they are Subhan Allah, Al-Hamdu Lillah, La ilaha illallah and Allahu Akbar. Ibn Jarir chose the view that they are {reward}all righteous deeds{/reward}.
now: You spend the evening on overtime for the kids' future and miss Maghrib. You worry about their grades more than your prayers. {idea}Your children are a blessing. The prayers are what stay with you.{/idea}
old: Providing more for my family is the best thing I can do.
new: Lasting deeds are better to hope in than anything I collect.
try: Say Subhan Allah, Al-Hamdu Lillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar ten times each today.

title: Mountains gone, earth flat, no one left behind.
subtitle: The Day when nothing can hide you
then: Ibn Kathir describes the earth that Day as {idea}clear and open, with nothing for anyone to hide behind{/idea}. Mujahid and Qatadah said no one will be hidden or absent. Allah will gather {trap}the first of them and the last of them, young or old{/trap}.
now: You keep a private browser, a locked phone, a version of yourself only you know. {idea}One day the ground goes flat and the cover is gone.{/idea} The good news: you can clean up what is behind the wall today.
old: What I keep hidden stays hidden.
new: Nothing will be hidden that Day. Better to fix it while I can.
try: Pick one hidden habit and take one small step away from it today, then ask Allah to forgive it.

title: You came back just as you were first made.
subtitle: The meeting you thought would never happen
then: All creation will stand before Allah, either in one row or in rows. Ibn Kathir calls His words {trap}a rebuke to those who denied the Hereafter{/trap}, before all creation: you did not think {idea}this would happen to you{/idea}.
now: You keep a careful diary for every meeting at work. Not one minute late. {idea}There is one meeting with your Lord that is already in the calendar{/idea}, and it is the only one you can never reschedule.
old: There is no appointment waiting for me after this life.
new: A meeting with my Lord is set. I want to arrive ready.
try: Spend five minutes tonight thinking about how you want that meeting to go.

title: A book that left out nothing, small or great.
subtitle: The record, and a Lord who is never unjust
then: The book records {trap}everything, major or minor{/trap}, with utmost precision. People will find everything, good and evil, present. Ibn Kathir stresses: {reward}He will overlook and forgive and have mercy{/reward}. He is the Judge who never wrongs, and doubles any good.
now: The rude reply you sent in the family chat. The coin you slipped into the charity box with no one watching. {idea}Both are written.{/idea} Your Lord wrongs no one, and doubles even a small good.
old: Small things do not count, good or bad.
new: Every small thing is written, and my Lord is fair and generous with it.
try: Do one tiny good deed today on purpose, knowing it is recorded.

title: Would you take your enemy as your friend?
subtitle: Iblis refused, and still people follow him
then: Allah reminds Adam's children of {trap}the enmity of Iblis towards them and their father{/trap}. Iblis was of the jinn, created from fire, and Ibn Kathir notes that when it matters, {idea}every vessel leaks what it contains{/idea}. He stepped beyond obedience. Yet people still take him as a friend.
now: The thought that says skip Fajr, just this once. The voice that says you deserve a look at that screen. {idea}It sounds like a friend. It is the oldest enemy you have.{/idea}
old: That inner voice is just me wanting what I want.
new: Some pulls come from an enemy who hates me. I do not have to follow him.
try: Next time a familiar bad urge comes today, say A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim and step away.

title: They were not there when the heavens were made.
subtitle: Why created things cannot be your helpers
then: Ibn Kathir explains: those taken as helpers instead of Allah {trap}are creatures just like you{/trap}. They did not exist when the heavens and earth were made. Allah says {idea}I am the One Who independently creates and controls all things{/idea}, with no partner or advisor. Malik said Adud means assistants.
now: You read your horoscope, check a lucky charm, or lean on a famous person's advice as if they hold the keys. {idea}They were not there at the beginning. They do not run anything.{/idea}
old: Some people or things have special pull over my fate.
new: Only the One who created everything controls it. Everyone else is created too.
try: Drop one small superstition or charm you lean on, and say a dua in its place.

title: Call your partners now. No answer comes.
subtitle: The silence of false supports
then: Allah will address the idolators before all creation: call those you claimed, to save you from where you are. They call, and {trap}they will not answer them{/trap}. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said Mawbiq means destruction, {trap}a gap neither side can cross{/trap}.
now: You text a friend at 2am in a crisis and they are asleep. The money in the account does not comfort you in the scan room. {idea}Allah is the One who always answers when you call.{/idea}
old: The things I lean on will come through when it matters.
new: Only Allah answers every call. I want to know Him before I need Him most.
try: Make one dua today in a calm moment, not only in crisis.

title: They see the Fire and know there is no way around it.
subtitle: When escape is no longer an option
then: Ibn Kathir says when they see it, {trap}they will realize that they cannot escape{/trap}, and that the anticipation and fear of punishment {trap}is in itself a real punishment{/trap}. They will have no way of fleeing.
now: Today you still have exits. You can turn back from the habit, apologize to the person, make wudu and pray. {idea}The way out is open right now, and it is wide.{/idea}
old: I will deal with my mistakes when I have to.
new: Today the door is open. Turning back is easy compared to the day it closes.
try: Say Astaghfirullah sincerely three times today for one specific thing.

title: Every example given, and still we argue most.
subtitle: The human habit of debating the truth

row.title: a clever excuse
sub: If Allah wills, He'll wake us

then: Allah has explained matters clearly, yet {trap}man is very quarrelsome and opposes truth with falsehood{/trap}. Ali reported the Prophet ﷺ visited him and Fatimah at night and asked if they would pray. Ali replied that their souls were in Allah's Hand. The Prophet ﷺ walked away {idea}slapping his thigh and reciting this verse{/idea}.
now: The alarm for Fajr goes off and your mind instantly builds a case: I am tired, Allah is merciful, I will make it up. {idea}You are arguing with the reminder instead of answering it.{/idea}
old: I have good reasons for not doing it right now.
new: Sometimes my reasons are just me arguing with a clear reminder.
try: The next time you catch yourself arguing against a good deed today, stop debating and do it.

title: What are they waiting for, the punishment itself?
subtitle: Guidance came, and they still held out
then: Ibn Kathir says nothing stopped them except {trap}their demand to witness with their own eyes the punishment{/trap} they were warned about. Past peoples said, bring it down on us. The Quraysh said, if this is true, rain stones on us. Yet {idea}guidance had already come to them{/idea}.
now: You keep saying you will get serious about prayer after a sign. After the health scare. After the funeral. {idea}The sign is already in your hands.{/idea} Asking forgiveness does not need a disaster first.
old: I will change when something big makes me.
new: Guidance is already here. I do not need to wait for a shock.
try: Ask Allah's forgiveness today for one thing, without waiting for a reason.

title: Messengers bring good news and warning. Some answer with mockery.
subtitle: Arguing to knock the truth down
then: Messengers come {reward}giving good news to those who believe{/reward} and warning those who reject. Some argue with falsehood {trap}to weaken the truth{/trap}, but cannot. Ibn Kathir calls making fun of Allah's signs {trap}the worst type of disbelief{/trap}.
now: Someone in the group chat posts a meme mocking prayer or hijab. Everyone sends laughing faces, and your thumb hovers over one too. {idea}Laughing along is a small step in the same direction.{/idea}
old: A joke about religion is just a joke.
new: Turning Allah's signs into a joke is never small.
try: Next time religion is mocked around you, simply do not join in. Silence is enough.

title: Reminded, he turned away and forgot his own deeds.
subtitle: The heart that closes after ignoring
then: Ibn Kathir explains the worst wrong is to be {trap}reminded of the signs of Allah and then turn away{/trap}, not listening or paying attention, while forgetting one's own bad deeds. Their hearts come to have coverings so {trap}they will not understand this Qur'an{/trap}.
now: The khutbah lands on you exactly, and you are checking your phone before the prayer ends. A friend gently names a habit and you change the subject. {idea}Every ignored reminder makes the next one harder to hear.{/idea}
old: I can ignore this reminder and catch the next one.
new: Each reminder I turn from makes my heart a little harder to reach.
try: Act on one reminder you received this week, however small, before tonight.

title: Your Lord is Forgiving, full of mercy, and patient.
subtitle: Why the punishment is not rushed
then: Right after the warning, Allah reminds His Messenger ﷺ that {reward}your Lord is forgiving and has great mercy{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says He is patient, conceals faults, forgives sins, and {idea}may guide some of them from wrongdoing to true guidance{/idea}. But the time is fixed.
now: You did something wrong years ago and nothing bad followed. You assumed it did not matter. {idea}Allah is not ignoring you. He is giving you room to come back.{/idea}
old: Nothing happened to me, so it must not matter.
new: The delay is mercy, giving me time to turn back.
try: Think of one past wrong you never repented for, and repent for it today.

title: Those towns had an appointed time too.
subtitle: Ruins as reminders
then: This refers to earlier nations destroyed {trap}because of their stubborn disbelief{/trap}, each with a set time limit. Ibn Kathir explains the address to the idolators of Makkah: {idea}you are not dearer to Us than them{/idea}, so beware.
now: It is easy to read about past nations and feel safe. {idea}The point is not them. It is you{/idea}, and the quiet belief that you are the exception to the rule.
old: Warnings in the Quran are about other people.
new: No one is dearer to Allah than His rules. I read these warnings for myself.
try: Read one warning verse today as if it was written to you personally.

title: A prophet sets out to learn, however long it takes.
subtitle: Musa's journey to someone who knew more
then: The Prophet ﷺ said Musa was asked who was the most learned, and said {trap}I am{/trap}. Allah rebuked him because {idea}he did not refer the knowledge to Allah{/idea}, and told him of a servant at the junction of the two seas who knew more. Musa set out with Yusha bin Nun, ready to travel even a lifetime.
now: You are the one at work everyone asks. You have answers for every family debate. {idea}The moment you feel you know the most is the moment to go and learn.{/idea}
old: I already know enough about this.
new: There is always someone who knows more. Knowledge belongs to Allah.
try: Ask someone today to teach you one thing you do not know, and listen fully.

title: At the meeting point, the fish slipped into the sea.
subtitle: The sign they were looking for, missed
then: Musa had been told that {idea}where you lose the fish, you will find him{/idea}. They slept at a rock. The fish moved, fell into the sea, and Allah held back the water so its path was {reward}like a tunnel{/reward}. They forgot it and walked on.
now: You were praying for direction and the answer came as an odd thing that went wrong. A cancelled flight, a missed bus, a closed door. {idea}Sometimes the sign is the thing you lost.{/idea}
old: Things going wrong are just bad luck.
new: A small loss can be the very sign I asked Allah for.
try: Think of one recent small loss and ask what it might be pointing you toward.

title: Past the right place, the tiredness hit.
subtitle: Fatigue as a signal
then: They walked the rest of the day and the whole night. The hadith says {idea}Musa did not feel tired until he passed the place Allah had ordered him to go to{/idea}. Then he said: bring our meal, {trap}we have suffered fatigue in this journey{/trap}.
now: You push through months at a job or a path that felt right, then suddenly everything drains you. {idea}Sometimes the exhaustion is a sign you have walked past where you were meant to stop.{/idea}
old: Feeling drained just means I need to push harder.
new: Sometimes tiredness is telling me to look back at where I missed the turn.
try: If something is draining you lately, sit quietly for five minutes and ask Allah where you should stop.

title: I forgot the fish, and owned up to it.
subtitle: Yusha admits his mistake
then: When Musa asked for the meal, Yusha told him plainly: {trap}I indeed forgot the fish{/trap}, and none but Shaytan made me forget to mention it. The hadith adds that the path was a tunnel for the fish and {idea}a wonder for Musa and his servant{/idea}.
now: You forgot to send the file, missed the deadline, left the stove on. Your boss asks. {idea}The honest I forgot is what lets the whole team turn back in time.{/idea}
old: Admitting my mistake will make things worse.
new: Owning a mistake quickly lets everyone get back on the right road.
try: Own up today to one small thing you forgot or got wrong, plainly and without excuses.

title: That is what we were seeking. So they went back.
subtitle: Turning around without blame
then: Musa did not scold Yusha. He heard the news and said, {idea}this is what we have been looking for{/idea}. Then {reward}they went back, following their own footprints{/reward}, to the rock.
now: Your child forgets something important and you feel the anger rise. Or you realize you took the wrong turn and the whole car is tense. {idea}Name it, turn around, and keep going together.{/idea}
old: When someone's mistake costs me, I need to make it clear.
new: The mistake showed the way. Turning back calmly is part of the journey.
try: When someone slips today, skip the blame and say: okay, let us go back and fix it.

title: They found a servant given mercy and knowledge from Allah.
subtitle: Meeting Al-Khidr
then: They found a man covered with a cloth at the rock. Ibn Kathir says this was {idea}Al-Khidr, as the authentic hadiths indicate{/idea}. Allah describes him first as one {reward}on whom We bestowed mercy{/reward}, then as one taught knowledge from Him.
now: You meet someone with a modest job who seems to see things you miss. No degree on the wall, but deep wisdom. {idea}Knowledge from Allah does not always come with a title.{/idea}
old: The wisest person is the one with the most qualifications.
new: Allah gives mercy and knowledge to whom He wills, often quietly.
try: Ask an older, quiet person in your life for one piece of advice this week.

title: May I follow you, so you can teach me?
subtitle: How a prophet asked to be taught
then: Ibn Kathir notes each had knowledge from Allah the other did not have. Musa's words were {idea}a question phrased in gentle terms, with no sense of force{/idea}, and he says this is {reward}the manner in which the seeker of knowledge should address the scholar{/reward}.
now: You message a teacher or a senior colleague with a one-line demand: explain this. {idea}Musa, a prophet who spoke with Allah, asked: may I follow you?{/idea} The way you ask shapes what you receive.
old: If I need knowledge, I can just demand it.
new: Learning starts with humility and a gentle request.
try: Ask someone a question today with may I or would you mind, and thank them after.

title: You will not be able to bear it with me.
subtitle: An honest warning before the journey
then: Al-Khidr explained that Musa would see him doing things that {trap}go against your law{/trap}. Ibn Kathir gives his meaning: {idea}I have knowledge from Allah that He has not taught you, and you have knowledge He has not taught me{/idea}. Each had his own responsibilities before Allah.
now: A mentor tells you up front: this will be harder than you think. You feel slightly insulted. {idea}An honest warning before a hard road is a kindness, not an insult.{/idea}
old: If someone says I cannot handle it, they are looking down on me.
new: An honest warning helps me prepare. It is not a judgment of my worth.
try: Thank someone today who once warned you honestly about something hard.

title: How can you be patient with what you cannot see?
subtitle: Patience and the hidden picture

row.title: I do not see it all

then: Ibn Kathir gives Al-Khidr's meaning: {trap}I know that you will denounce me justifiably{/trap}, but {idea}I have knowledge of Allah's wisdom and the hidden interests which I can see but you cannot{/idea}.
now: A rejection letter, a diagnosis, a move you did not want. You have one frame of a long film. {idea}Impatience is often just the pain of not seeing the whole picture.{/idea}
old: If I cannot see a reason, there is no reason.
new: Allah sees what I cannot. Patience means trusting the part I do not see.
try: Name one thing you are impatient with right now and say: Allah sees what I do not.

title: You will find me patient, if Allah wills.
subtitle: A sincere promise that leaned on Allah
then: Musa answered: {idea}if Allah wills, you will find me patient{/idea} with whatever I see, and {reward}I will not go against you in anything{/reward}. Just verses earlier, Allah taught to say If Allah wills about the future.
now: Before a new diet, a new job, a new routine of reading Quran, you say: I will definitely stick to it. {idea}Make the promise and tie it to Allah's help, not just your willpower.{/idea}
old: If I want it badly enough, I will keep my promise.
new: I promise sincerely and lean on Allah to help me keep it.
try: Make one small promise to yourself today, say In sha Allah, and ask Allah to help you keep it.

title: Do not ask until I bring it up.
subtitle: The one condition
then: Al-Khidr set a condition: {idea}do not initiate any discussion of the matter{/idea}, until I raise it with you before you ask. The explanation was promised, but {reward}in its own time{/reward}.
now: You want to know right now why the job fell through, why the marriage is delayed, why the test result came back like that. {idea}Some answers come only after the journey.{/idea}
old: I need the explanation now or I cannot go on.
new: Some explanations come later. I can keep walking without them.
try: Write down one why you are carrying, and leave it with Allah for now.

title: He damaged the boat that gave them a free ride.
subtitle: The first test of patience
then: The crew recognized Al-Khidr and {reward}let them ride free of charge{/reward}. Far from shore, he pulled out one of the planks and patched it. Musa could not restrain himself: {trap}have you damaged it so its people will drown?{/trap} Qatadah said Imr means an astounding thing.
now: Your car breaks down on the way to an important meeting. A kind neighbor's shop is hit by bad luck. {idea}It looks like pure loss from where you stand.{/idea} The story is not finished yet.
old: When something bad happens to good people, it makes no sense.
new: What looks like damage may hold a reason I have not been told yet.
try: When something breaks today, wait one hour before deciding it was all bad.

title: Did I not tell you that you would not manage it?
subtitle: A calm reminder of the agreement
then: Al-Khidr did not defend himself. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}this thing I did deliberately{/idea} was one of the things I told you not to denounce, because {trap}you do not know the full story{/trap}, and there is a reason you do not know.
now: A grandparent makes a decision that looks wrong, and you start lecturing. They only say: wait, you will see. {idea}Not every decision owes you an explanation in the moment.{/idea}
old: Anyone who does something odd must explain it to me right away.
new: Sometimes the right response is to remember I do not know the whole story.
try: Hold back one judgment today about something you only half understand.

title: Do not hold my forgetting against me.
subtitle: Asking for gentleness after a slip
then: Musa asked him not to call him to account for what he forgot, meaning {reward}do not be harsh with me{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith: {idea}the first time, Musa asked because he had forgotten his promise{/idea}.
now: You snap at your spouse again after promising you would not. You feel like a failure. {idea}Say sorry, ask for gentleness, and try again.{/idea} Even a prophet slipped from forgetting.
old: If I break a promise once, I have proven I am hopeless.
new: Forgetting is human. I can apologize, ask for patience, and keep going.
try: Apologize simply today for one small slip, without overexplaining.

title: The second event was far harder to accept.
subtitle: A loss Musa could not bear to see
then: Musa objected {trap}even more fervently than in the first case{/trap}: you have taken an innocent soul, a young person who had done nothing wrong. Al-Khidr acted on knowledge given him by Allah, which is not given to anyone today. {idea}The reason is told later in the surah.{/idea}
now: A child dies in the hospital ward down the corridor from you. Nothing about it feels fair, and you cannot find words. {idea}Musa felt that too. Grief and protest are human.{/idea} Allah's knowledge holds what yours cannot.
old: If a loss makes no sense to me, it makes no sense at all.
new: Some losses I will never understand here. Allah knows what I cannot.
try: Make dua today for one family you know that is grieving a loss.

title: Did I not tell you? This time, more firmly.
subtitle: The second reminder
then: Once again, Ibn Kathir notes, {idea}Al-Khidr reiterates the condition set in the first place{/idea}. The words are nearly the same as before, now said directly to Musa, a reminder that he had agreed to wait.
now: The same lesson keeps finding you: the same kind of argument with your parent, the same money stress at the end of every month. {idea}When a reminder repeats, it is asking you to finally hear it.{/idea}
old: I have heard this lesson before. It does not apply anymore.
new: A repeated reminder is a sign I have not yet learned it.
try: Name one lesson life keeps repeating to you, and write one way to act on it.

title: If I ask again, part ways with me.
subtitle: Musa sets his own limit
then: Musa said that if he objected again, {trap}keep me not in your company{/trap}, for you have accepted my apology twice. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}may the mercy of Allah be upon us and upon Musa. If he had stayed with his companion he would have seen wonders{/reward}.
now: You quit the class, the halaqa, the friendship one complaint too early. {idea}A little more patience might have shown you wonders.{/idea}
old: If it is frustrating, I should walk away.
new: Patience a little longer can open a door to things I would never see otherwise.
try: Give one thing you were about to quit one more honest try this week.

title: Refused food, he still fixed their wall for free.
subtitle: Good done for people who were unkind
then: The hadith calls the townspeople {trap}mean, miserly{/trap}: they refused to feed two hungry travelers. Yet Al-Khidr found a wall about to collapse and {reward}set it up with his own hands{/reward}. Musa said, since they did not host us, you should not work for them for free.
now: The neighbor who never says hello needs help with their fence. The coworker who took credit for your work is stuck on a task. {idea}You can do good without waiting for them to deserve it.{/idea}
old: I only owe kindness to people who are kind to me.
new: Good done for Allah does not wait for the other person to earn it.
try: Do one helpful thing today for someone who has not been kind to you.

title: This is where we part. Now hear the meaning.
subtitle: The explanations are coming
then: Musa had said that if he asked again, they would part. So Al-Khidr said: {trap}this is the parting of the ways{/trap}. But he did not leave Musa confused. {reward}I will tell you the interpretation{/reward} of the things you could not be patient with.
now: A hard season ends. A job, a move, a relationship. {idea}Sometimes the meaning only arrives at the parting.{/idea} Looking back, the pieces begin to fit.
old: If it ended badly, none of it made sense.
new: Endings can be where the meaning finally shows itself.
try: Look back at one hard chapter that ended, and write one good thing it brought you.

title: A damaged boat was the one the king did not take.
subtitle: The first hidden reason
then: Allah showed Al-Khidr the hidden reasons. A king who was {trap}one of the oppressors{/trap} seized every good boat by force. Making it look faulty meant {reward}its poor owners who had nothing else could benefit from it{/reward}. It was also said they were orphans.
now: You did not get the bigger flat, the flashier job, the car you wanted. Years later you see what that bigger thing would have cost you. {idea}A small dent can keep the whole boat safe.{/idea}
old: Every setback is just a loss.
new: Some damage is protection I cannot see yet.
try: Recall one past disappointment that later turned out to protect you, and thank Allah for it.

title: His believing parents were spared what was coming.
subtitle: The second hidden reason
then: Their love for him {trap}might make them follow him in disbelief{/trap}. Qatadah said his parents rejoiced at his birth and grieved at his death, and had he lived he would have caused their ruin. He said: {reward}let a man be content with the decree of Allah{/reward}. The hadith says Allah decrees nothing for the believer except it is good for him.
now: You lost something you loved and begged Allah to keep. You still miss it. {idea}You may never see the reason in this life.{/idea} But the believer's loss is never wasted with Allah.
old: If Allah took it, He must not care about me.
new: Allah's decree for a believer is good, even when it breaks my heart.
try: Say Alhamdulillah ala kulli hal, praise to Allah in every state, once today about something painful.

title: A better child, nearer to mercy, in his place.
subtitle: Loss followed by replacement
then: Ibn Jurayj explained the replacement: {reward}a child who was better than this one, a child for whom they would feel more compassion{/reward}. The grief was real. So was {idea}what their Lord intended for them next{/idea}.
now: After a miscarriage, a lost job, a friendship that ended, the space feels empty for a long time. {idea}Allah does not take from a believer without intending something good to follow.{/idea}
old: What I lost can never be replaced.
new: Allah can give me something better after loss, in His timing.
try: Make dua today: O Allah, reward me in my loss and give me better after it.

title: Their father was righteous, so Allah guarded their treasure.
subtitle: The third hidden reason

row.title: mercy from your Lord
sub: I did it not of myself

then: Ibn Kathir says this shows {reward}a righteous person's offspring will be taken care of{/reward}, and the blessing of his worship extends to them. Ibn Abbas noted it is not said the boys themselves were righteous. Al-Khidr ended: all three were {idea}mercy from your Lord, and I did them not of my own accord{/idea}.
now: You pray at night when the house is asleep, give quietly, keep your word at work. You worry what will become of your kids. {idea}Your goodness today may be the wall that guards them long after you.{/idea}
old: My children's future depends only on what I leave them in money.
new: My righteousness can protect my children in ways I will never see.
try: Do one good deed today with the intention that Allah protects your family through it.

title: They asked about Dhul-Qarnayn. Here is his story.
subtitle: The third question answered
then: The disbelievers of Makkah had asked the People of the Book for questions to test the Prophet ﷺ. One was {idea}a man who traveled extensively throughout the earth{/idea}. The answer came as revelation: {reward}say, I will recite to you something of his story{/reward}.
now: You search for answers about life in ten browser tabs and three podcasts. {idea}The Quran says: I will recite to you.{/idea} Some answers are given, not found.
old: I have to find every answer myself.
new: Allah has already recited some answers. I can start there.
try: Before searching online about a big question today, read what the Quran says on it first.

title: Allah gave him power and the means to everything.
subtitle: Strength handed to a king
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gave him {reward}great power{/reward}, armies and equipment, with dominion over east and west. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the means of everything meant {idea}knowledge{/idea}. Notice the verbs: {idea}We established, We gave{/idea}.
now: You got the promotion, the team, the budget. You have more say over people than ever before. {idea}It was handed to you, and it will be asked about.{/idea}
old: My position is mine because I earned it.
new: Any power I hold was given to me by Allah, as a trust.
try: Use whatever authority you have today, at home or work, to make one person's day easier.

title: He used the means. He followed a way.
subtitle: Gifts are meant to be used
then: Only three words: so he followed a way. Ibn Abbas said {idea}he followed different routes to achieve what he wanted{/idea}. Qatadah said he followed {idea}the routes and landmarks of the earth{/idea}. He was given the means, and he used them.
now: You have a skill you have not touched in years. A language, an instrument, a talent for teaching. {idea}A gift left unused is still a gift, but it does no good sitting on the shelf.{/idea}
old: Having a talent is enough.
new: A gift from Allah is meant to be used on a path.
try: Spend twenty minutes today using one skill you have been neglecting.

title: At the far west, he was given a choice about a people.
subtitle: Power tested by choice

row.title: the far west
sub: sun seems to set in the sea

then: He reached the furthest point west and {idea}saw the sun as if it were setting in the ocean{/idea}, as anyone on a coast sees. Ibn Kathir calls tales of him reaching where the sun sets in the sky {trap}not true at all{/trap}. There Allah gave him power over a people, and a choice, and {reward}his justice and faith became apparent{/reward}.
now: You are the older sibling, the manager, the parent. Someone under you messes up and you can go hard or go gentle. {idea}What you do when you could do anything shows who you are.{/idea}
old: Having power means I can do what I want.
new: Power is a test of whether I choose justice and goodness.
try: Next time you have the upper hand with someone today, choose the kinder fair option.

title: The one who does wrong answers here and to his Lord.
subtitle: Justice that remembers the Hereafter

row.title: Allah
sub: he will be returned to Him

then: His answer showed {reward}his justice and faith{/reward}. He would act against the one who {trap}persists in his disbelief and wrongdoing{/trap}, then that person would be returned to his Lord. Ibn Kathir notes this {idea}implies a confirmation of the Hereafter{/idea}, even in a king's words.
now: You get away with a shortcut at work and the boss never finds out. {idea}Earthly accounts are not the final ones.{/idea} The verse is a mirror: every one of us will be returned to our Lord.
old: If no one catches me, there is no consequence.
new: Even if I escape here, I am returned to my Lord.
try: Correct one small wrong of yours today that no one else knows about.

title: For the one who believes and does good: ease and kind words.
subtitle: How a just leader treats the good
then: For the one who believes, the reward is {reward}the best reward in the Hereafter, with Allah{/reward}. And from the king himself: {idea}we shall speak to him mild words{/idea}. Mujahid said: words of kindness.
now: The reliable colleague, the child who does what you ask, the spouse who never complains. {idea}They are the easiest to forget to thank.{/idea} Ease and gentle words are their due.
old: The good ones do not need my attention.
new: The ones doing good deserve my gentleness and ease most of all.
try: Thank the most reliable person in your life today in specific, gentle words.

title: Then he followed another way.
subtitle: After one task, the next
then: Ibn Kathir says he then {idea}traveled from the west of the earth towards the east{/idea}. Each time he passed a nation, {reward}he called them to Allah{/reward}. One mission completed simply led into the next.
now: You finished Ramadan strong, then the next month you stopped. You memorized one surah, then shelved the rest. {idea}The verse just says: then he followed another way.{/idea}
old: I have done my good deed. I can rest now.
new: Each good done opens the next road. I keep following it.
try: Pick the next small step after something good you recently finished, and start it today.

title: A people with nothing to shade them from the sun.
subtitle: In the far east
then: He reached the place where the sun rises and found a people with {trap}no buildings or trees to cover them and shade them from the heat{/trap}. Qatadah said it was mentioned they lived in a land where {trap}nothing grew{/trap}, sheltering until the sun passed its peak.
now: You complain the air conditioning is weak, that the flat is small. {idea}A roof and shade are blessings most people in history did not have.{/idea}
old: Shelter and comfort are just normal.
new: A roof over my head is a gift I easily forget.
try: Thank Allah today for your roof, then give something toward someone's shelter.

title: So it was. And We knew all that he had.
subtitle: Nothing about him was hidden
then: Mujahid and As-Suddi said this means {idea}Allah knew everything about him and his army, and nothing was hidden from Him{/idea}, even though they came from many nations and lands. As the verse says: {idea}nothing is hidden from Allah, in the earth or in the heaven{/idea}.
now: You are one face in a city of millions, one of a thousand employees. You feel lost in the crowd. {idea}Allah knows all that you have, all you do, all you carry.{/idea}
old: I am too small to be noticed in all of this.
new: Allah encompasses all of it, and me in it.
try: Tonight, tell Allah about one thing you did today that no one noticed.

title: Then he followed a third way.
subtitle: West, east, and now between the mountains

row.title: a new test
sub: a new chance to do good

then: For the third time the verse says: then he followed a way. Ibn Kathir says he traveled from the east until he reached {idea}a place between two mountains with a valley in between{/idea}, from which Yajuj and Majuj would come to {trap}spread mischief, destroying crops and people{/trap}.
now: Every new phase of life, a new city, a new job, a new child, is another road. {idea}Each one carries its own test and its own chance to do good.{/idea}
old: Once I settle, the tests will stop.
new: Every new road brings a new test, and a new chance to serve.
try: In the newest situation you are in, name one way you can be useful to the people there.

title: A people he could barely understand, still worth helping.
subtitle: Language is no barrier to justice
then: Ibn Kathir says he found a people whose speech he could not understand, {idea}because they were so isolated from other people{/idea}. Even so, they made their need known and {reward}he listened{/reward}.
now: The new family on your street whose language you do not speak. The elderly patient at the clinic who cannot fill in the form. {idea}A barrier of language is not a barrier to kindness.{/idea}
old: If we cannot communicate, I cannot really help.
new: I can still listen and help across a language gap.
try: Help one person today who struggles to communicate, with patience, a smile, or a translation app.

title: They offered to pay him for a barrier.
subtitle: A people asking for protection
then: They told him Yajuj and Majuj were {trap}doing great mischief in the land{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said they wanted to {reward}collect money among themselves to give to him{/reward} so he would build a barrier.
now: Someone asks you for help and quickly offers to pay, almost embarrassed to ask. {idea}How you respond tells them what kind of person you are.{/idea}
old: People in need should pay for the help they get.
new: When I have the power to help, the help itself is the good deed.
try: Help someone today who would have offered to pay, and refuse the payment kindly.

title: What my Lord gave me is better. Just lend me your hands.
subtitle: Turning down the money, asking for effort
then: He answered {reward}with kindness, righteousness and good intentions{/reward}: the power Allah has given me is better than what you collected. Like Sulayman, who said what Allah gave me is better. But he asked them to {idea}help with your labor and equipment{/idea}.
now: A friend in trouble wants you to fix everything and offers a gift. {idea}Refuse the gift, then invite them to work beside you.{/idea} People are lifted by building, not by being carried.
old: Helping someone means doing it all for them.
new: The best help asks nothing in return and invites people to build with me.
try: Next time you help someone today, invite them to do one part with you.

title: Iron blocks, fire, and molten copper poured on top.
subtitle: Building the barrier step by step
then: Ibn Kathir explains he stacked iron blocks {idea}starting at the bottom, until he reached the tops of the mountains{/idea}. Then he lit a fire until it was burning hot. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the poured metal was {reward}copper{/reward}, some adding molten.
now: Your plan to protect your family from bad habits: limits on screens, time to pray together, honest talks. {idea}One block at a time, heated and sealed. Protection is built, not wished for.{/idea}
old: If I trust Allah, I do not need to plan carefully.
new: Trust in Allah goes with skill, method, and hard work.
try: Write down three concrete steps to protect one thing you care about, and do the first today.

title: They could not climb it, and could not dig through.
subtitle: A barrier that held
then: Ibn Kathir notes the verb for digging is stronger than for climbing, {idea}reflecting the difficulty of the action{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ once woke saying a hole had opened in the barrier, and when asked if they would be destroyed with righteous people among them, he said: {trap}yes, if evil increases{/trap}.
now: You build good walls around your home: a routine, good company, prayer on time. {idea}Walls hold, but the Prophet ﷺ warned what happens when evil increases inside.{/idea}
old: Once I am protected, I can stop paying attention.
new: Protection holds while I keep the good growing and the evil small.
try: Remove one small source of bad influence from your home or phone today.

title: This is a mercy from my Lord, not my achievement.
subtitle: A builder who gave the credit away
then: After building it, he said: {reward}this is a mercy from my Lord{/reward} for the people. Yet he knew it would not last forever: when the promise comes, it will be flattened to the ground, and {idea}the promise of my Lord is ever true{/idea}.
now: You finish the project, the house, the degree. People congratulate you. {idea}Compare the man of the two gardens with this king.{/idea} One said I, the other said my Lord.
old: What I built is my achievement, and it will last.
new: What I built is a mercy from Allah, and it will last only as long as He wills.
try: When someone praises your work today, answer with: Alhamdulillah, it is from Allah.

title: People surging like waves, then the Horn is blown.
subtitle: The barrier falls, the gathering begins
then: Ibn Kathir says this will happen before the Day of Resurrection and after the Dajjal. The Prophet ﷺ said the angel of the Horn already has it in his mouth, waiting for the command. When asked what to say, he taught: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs{/reward}.
now: The news feels like it is surging over you. Wars, prices, illness, headlines one after another. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ gave his companions words for this exact feeling.{/idea}
old: When the world feels like it is falling apart, I have nowhere to stand.
new: Allah is enough for me, and He is the best One to trust with all of it.
try: Say Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil the next time the news makes you anxious today.

title: That Day, Hell is shown openly to those who rejected.
subtitle: What was ignored becomes visible
then: Allah tells us He will {trap}bring it forth for them to see before they enter it{/trap}, which will intensify their distress. The Prophet ﷺ described Hell being brought forth by angels. What was warned about in words becomes {trap}plain to view{/trap}.
now: You read the warnings in the Quran and scroll past them to the comforting verses. {idea}The warnings are shown to you now in words, so you never have to see them any other way.{/idea}
old: I would rather not think about the Fire at all.
new: Allah shows me the warning now so I can stay far from it.
try: Ask Allah tonight: O Allah, protect me from the Fire, three times, with presence.

title: Their eyes were covered from My reminder.
subtitle: Turning a blind eye and a deaf ear
then: Ibn Kathir explains they {trap}neglected it, turning a blind eye and a deaf ear{/trap}, refusing guidance. He cites the verse that whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious is given a devil as a companion. {idea}The covering began with their own looking away.{/idea}
now: You keep the Quran app on the last screen of your phone, behind the games. Every time the reminder pops up, you swipe it away. {idea}Small swipes become a covering over the eyes.{/idea}
old: I am not rejecting anything. I am just busy.
new: Looking away again and again can harden into not seeing at all.
try: Move your Quran app to your home screen today and open it once.

title: Do they think Allah's servants can protect them from Him?
subtitle: Taking created beings as protectors
then: Ibn Kathir asks for them: {trap}do they think this is right for them and that it is going to benefit them?{/trap} He cites the verse that those taken as protectors {trap}will deny their worship of them, and become opponents to them{/trap}.
now: You lean on a respected elder, a scholar, a charismatic figure, so much that their word feels like a guarantee. {idea}They are servants too.{/idea} Love them, learn from them, but your safety is with Allah alone.
old: If I stay close to the right person, I will be safe.
new: Even the best people are Allah's servants. Only He can protect me.
try: Make one dua today directly to Allah for something you usually ask someone else to pray for.

title: Shall we tell you who loses the most from their deeds?
subtitle: A question to stop and ask yourself
then: Companions differed over which groups this verse covers. Ibn Kathir concludes {idea}the Ayah is general{/idea}, since it came in Makkah before those groups were even addressed. It refers to {trap}everyone who worships Allah in a way that is not acceptable, thinking that he is right{/trap}.
now: You read this verse and immediately think of someone else. A cousin, a sect, a type of person online. {idea}The verse asks you to look at your own deeds first.{/idea}
old: This verse is about people who are clearly wrong.
new: The greatest losers think they are winning. I must check myself.
try: Pick one regular deed you do, and ask honestly: is this for Allah and in the way He taught?
