title: Busy all their lives, sure they were doing well.
subtitle: Effort that was lost without them knowing
then: Ibn Kathir says these did {trap}deeds that do not count, not in accordance with the prescribed way acceptable to Allah{/trap}. Yet {trap}they thought there was some basis for their deeds and that they were accepted and loved{/trap}. He likens it to a mirage that the thirsty think is water.
now: You are exhausted from a week of running around: work, events, causes, volunteering. All good. {idea}Busy is not the same as accepted.{/idea} Stop once in a while and ask what it is all for.
old: If I am working hard and feel good about it, I must be doing well.
new: Effort counts when it rests on the right intention and the right way.
try: Take ten quiet minutes this week to review what you spend your effort on, and why.

title: No weight on the scale for those who denied the meeting.
subtitle: When deeds are emptied of value
then: They denied the proofs of His Oneness and {trap}denied the Hereafter{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}We will not make their Balance heavy because it is empty of any goodness{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said a huge man may come that Day weighing no more than a gnat's wing with Allah.
now: Big titles, big following, big donations with your name on the wall. {idea}Weight on the Day comes from faith and sincerity, not from size.{/idea} A quiet deed done for Him may outweigh all of it.
old: Big, visible deeds weigh the most.
new: What gives a deed weight is believing in the meeting and doing it for Allah.
try: Do one small good deed today with the meeting with Allah clearly in mind.

title: Their recompense came from denial and mockery.
subtitle: Taking the signs and messengers as a joke
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the punishment {trap}because of their disbelief and because they took the signs and Messengers of Allah as a joke{/trap}, mocking them and disbelieving them in the worst way. The verse links the end to what was chosen.
now: The sarcastic comment about the imam's khutbah. The laugh at someone trying to practice. {idea}Mockery feels light in the moment. The verse shows how heavy it is.{/idea}
old: Laughing at religious things is harmless.
new: Mocking Allah's signs is a choice with real weight.
try: If you have joked about something sacred recently, ask Allah's forgiveness for it today.

title: For those who believe and do good: Firdaws as their welcome.
subtitle: The highest garden, offered as hospitality
then: Qatadah said Al-Firdaws is {reward}a hill in Paradise, at its center, the best of it{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}if you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for Al-Firdaws{/idea}, the highest part, from which the rivers of Paradise spring. It is given as hospitality, a host's welcome.
now: You ask Allah for small things: pass the exam, find parking, make the meeting go well. {idea}He invites you to ask for the very highest.{/idea}
old: I am not good enough to ask for the highest Paradise.
new: The Prophet ﷺ told me to ask for Firdaws. So I ask.
try: In your next dua, say: O Allah, I ask You for Al-Firdaws al-Ala.

title: Forever there, and never wanting to leave.
subtitle: A home you will never tire of
then: Ibn Kathir notes one might imagine that {trap}a person who stays in one place forever would get tired and bored of it{/trap}. But Allah tells us {reward}they will never choose to change or move from where they are{/reward}.
now: The new phone gets boring in a month. The dream holiday ends with you scrolling in the hotel. You always want the next thing. {idea}Imagine a place where that restless wanting finally stops.{/idea}
old: Nothing could keep me happy forever.
new: Paradise is the one place where I will never want anything else.
try: Notice one moment of restlessness today and remind yourself what it points toward.

title: If the sea were ink, it would run dry first.
subtitle: The words of Allah never end
then: After the stories of the Cave, the gardens, Musa and Dhul-Qarnayn, the surah widens out. Even with sea after sea as ink, {idea}the Words of Allah would still never run out{/idea}. Ar-Rabi bin Anas said all mankind's knowledge next to Allah's is like {idea}a drop of water compared to all the oceans{/idea}.
now: You feel you have figured life out, or that you never will. Libraries, search engines, whole careers of study. {idea}It is all one drop.{/idea} There is always more of Allah to learn about.
old: I have learned most of what there is to know about my faith.
new: Allah's words are endless. I will always have more to learn and wonder at.
try: Stand by water today, a tap, a river, the sea, and recall this verse.

title: Hoping to meet your Lord? Do good, for Him alone.
subtitle: The closing summary of the surah
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say: I am only a man like you, and I knew the stories of the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn {idea}only because Allah made them known to me{/idea}. Ibn Kathir names the two features of an accepted deed: {reward}for Allah alone, and in the way of the Messenger ﷺ{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ said what he feared most for us was showing off.
now: You post the iftar you served, mention the charity in passing, pray a little longer when someone is watching. {idea}On that Day, it will be said: go to the ones you showed off for.{/idea} Do it for Him and it is safe.
old: It does not matter who sees my good deeds.
new: A deed is safe when it is for Allah alone and done His Messenger's ﷺ way.
try: Do one good deed today that only Allah will ever know about.
